seed.caption_html: Reweight your portfolio and see how the risk changes. Edit any New % cell up or down, or set a holding to 0 to drop it — then Run to compare current vs simulated on the same EWMA + Ledoit-Wolf covariance engine as the Risk Contribution tab. The optimizer console below suggests constrained allocations and sweeps the cap and return trade-offs. Inherits the Account / Asset-class filters.

grid.caption_html: Edit any New % cell to move weight between holdings, or set one to 0 to drop it. Simulated weights must total 100% before you can Run.

optimizer.caption_html: Two one-click weightings — covariance only, no expected-return guesses. Min-variance: the lowest-volatility mix subject to the per-name cap and per-class floors. Risk-parity: equal risk contribution from every holding — inherently diversifying, subject to the same per-name cap. Fills the grid below; review and Run. In-sample optimization on the trailing-window covariance — no transaction costs, and the estimates carry sampling error, so treat as direction, not precision. Holdings too young to model are carried at their current weight and excluded from the vol estimate.

headline.caption_html: Cards show the after value with Δ vs before; green = improved. Lower is better for vol / down-β / concentration; higher Effective N and Diversification Ratio are better. Sharpe uses a 3-month-Treasury RF baseline. Sortino, VaR/CVaR, correlations and stressed DR are in the detail panels below.

diversification.dr_note_html: DR is the no-diversification baseline divided by realized portfolio vol; >1 means correlations are reducing total risk below the weighted-average standalone vol.

stress.caption_html: Stress days (SPY log-return z ≤ −1.50): before = 0/607, after = 0/607. Spearman correlation is used inside the stress-day matrix to stay robust on small samples.

frontier.caption_html: Each marker is one constrained solve at a different risk aversion; the line runs from the minimum-variance end to the maximum-return end, under your live constraints (per-name cap 71%, floors: equity 86%, fixed income 0%). Expected returns are CAPM-implied estimates, not forecasts: E[r] = rf + β × ERP with rf = 4.0% (FRED DGS3MO), ERP = 4.5%, β fitted on 5 years of daily returns vs the Fama-French market factor. β = 1.0 assumed (no fitted regression) for: SGOV. Young holdings held at current weight. ★ = current book. The equal-risk-contribution marker is traced without class floors — like the tab's risk-parity optimizer — so it can sit outside the frontier's feasible set.
